results.title: Aiming Thinking: A Metacognitive Framework for Human-AI ...
results.content: To bridge this cognitive gap, this paper proposes and formalizes Aiming Thinking (AT), a metacognitive framework designed specifically to structure the process of co-creation with generative AI. Aiming Thinking: The Metathinking Framework for the AI Era. The limitations of Level 2 frameworks in the context of generative AI reveal a critical need for a new cognitive layer—a methodology designed not to solve a domain-specific problem, but to orchestrate the problem-solving process with an AI partner. Each scenario focuses on a specific Level 2 framework and contrasts a traditional, human-only approach with an augmented approach using Aiming Thinking (AT) and a generative AI partner. By defining its four pillars—Targeting, Trajectory Design, Sequencing, and Calibration—and providing a foundational library of 20 actionable patterns, we have moved beyond the dark art of prompt engineering to establish a systematic, teachable, and robust framework for human-AI collaboration.

results.title: Evaluating AI-Powered Applications for Enhancing Undergraduate ...
results.content: # Evaluating AI-Powered Applications for Enhancing Undergraduate Students’ Metacognitive Strategies, Self-Determined Motivation, and Social Learning in English Language Education. This study investigates the effectiveness of AI-powered educational applications in enhancing metacognitive and social learning strategies, as well as self-determined motivation, among Chinese undergraduate students. However, research examining the direct effects of AI-powered applications on EAP learners’ metacognitive and social learning strategies and self-determined motivation remains limited. Specifically, the research seeks to investigate (1) the effect of AI-powered applications on EAP learners’ metacognitive strategies, (2) the impact of AI-powered applications on undergraduate students’ use of social learning strategies, and (3) the influence of AI-powered applications on students’ self-determined motivation. In summary, the study demonstrates that AI-powered tools, when thoughtfully integrated into language learning contexts, can significantly enhance metacognitive strategies, social strategies, and motivation. Evaluating AI-Powered Applications for Enhancing Undergraduate Students’ Metacognitive Strategies, Self-Determined Motivation, and Social Learning in English Language Education.

results.title: Full article: Generative AI in Human-AI Collaboration: Validation of ...
results.content: While there is currently no validated instrument specifically designed to measure metacognitive engagement during collaboration with AI systems, the Meta AI Literacy Scale (MAILS) scale (Carolus et al., Citation2023b) makes a noteworthy contribution by incorporating psychological dimensions relevant to long-term AI use. Because existing measures of general AI Literacy do not include items that directly assess the ability to communicate and coordinate with an AI system, they should not be as effective at predicting the benefits experienced from working with collaborative AI tools. The Collaborative AI Literacy measure is required when the goal is to evaluate readiness for AI-integrated workflows or roles, design professional development programs that include interaction with generative or decision-support AI tools, or assess performance and cognitive engagement in collaborative human-AI tasks. The development and validation of the Collaborative AI Literacy and Metacognition scales represents a significant step forward in identifying and assessing the skills required to work with collaborative AI tools such as generative AI.
